newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia gives ship import permits to 28 firms.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia gives ship import permits to 28 firms.

text.p: Indonesia's government has awarded licences to 28 companies to import fishing vessels, the Bisnis Indonesia daily reported on Thursday.
"Among those 28 companies, 24 of them are allowed to import 302 second-hand fishing vessels," Director-General of Fisheries F.X Murdjijo was quoted as saying.
Murdjijo said the remaining four companies obtained government licences to import 18 new fishing vessels.
He said the permission was given in a decree from the agriculture minister dated February 4 but he declined to name the companies involved.
The paper said the import licences were effective until December 1997.
An agriculture ministry official told Reuters on Thursday that the government was likely to announce the ruling later this month after the Eid Al-Fitr Moslem celebration on the weekend.
"It is still being discussed if the ruling will be under a ministrial decree or a presidential decree because it also concerns other departments such as customs and excise," he added.

Bisnis Indonesia quoted its sources as saying that PT Daya Guna Samudera was licenced to import 60 fishing vessels -- the largest portion -- without giving details if they were new or second-hand vessels.

"We cannot comment on that news. We have not yet received any letter or news from the agriculture department. It's better to wait," Dixi Satyanagara, deputy corporate secretary of Daya Guna Samudera, told Reuters.
Satyanagara declined to comment on the number of vessels the company had asked to import.
By the lunch break, shares of Daya Guna Samudera topped the active list with 3.1 million shares traded, rising 100 rupiah to 3,750 rupiah.
